items.title: Harrison Verrett Interview, 1961-08-10
items.q: since you were mostly associated with Pat Stomino

ctx.x: Yeah, if he's not experiencing nothing. Yeah. See, like Lewis Nelson, he likes that. He likes what? He likes for you to move, yeah. Oh, he does? Yeah, he got a good sense of hearing for cards, you see. You can move, he can tell if he can make a seventh or ninth or something like that. He can make it around with a trombone. He's a good musician, yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.

I was going to ask what I think of it, since you were mostly associated with Pat Stomino, not that he's a real old-time musician and all that, and one of the old pioneers of the Dixie thing, but I wondered about your reactions to the rock and roll. What made him so sensational? Did you ever figure it out? Well, the rock and roll that came from Alan Freed, he does...
